_about.names: Monster_eng.gmd (arc/ID/ID_arena_eng) string at index = the em number. The index rule matches every archive checked by eye but is NOT yet confirmed from the code.
_about.hideIdx: mesh-table +0 bit 0 clear (the MHGU draw-mask field; in 3U it is clear on exactly the group 100-106 rows). The 3U draw code that tests it has not been read.
_about.small: the per-enemy record's flags word bit 0 (mh3u_species.is_large): clear on every monster the Monster List files small and set on every one it files large or elder, across all 72 rows, the one exception being Abyssal Lagiacrus, whose row says small and whose own flag says large. The quest code reads the bit as a monster flag (0x5bd094, 0x856e30); its name is not decoded.
_about.sizeBase: 1.0: the monster size tables are not decoded for 3U.
_about.groups: null: 3U ships no part-visibility (.mpm) file; see partTable.

_about.partTable: the per-enemy parts table in the executable (mh3u_parts.py): 0xc1c008[em] -> record +0x90, 0x14-byte rows [part, group, cond, mode, param, threshold]; group 255 = the monster's own model, n = the severed piece with that `group`. uEnemy re-applies it every frame (0x82ebd4 -> 0x5c5568 -> 0x852118); a part no row names stays drawn. Parts a monster class sets in its own code are in partCode instead (mh3u_parts_class.py: the same row form, class conditions from 100).
_about.boneNodes: every bone node of the model as [three.js name, global bone id, is a _s leaf] -- the whole skeleton, not only the skinned joints, so a severed piece can be attached to the body by global bone id (the body may not skin a gid its piece does).
_about.species: the game's own: the Monster List table in the executable (mh3u_species.py, 72 six-byte rows at 0xba338c, the lookup 0x59ca54) gives each monster a species 0-11. `speciesAbbr` is the label the game itself prints for it (Monster_eng.gmd 128 + species, per 0x9545d0) -- BrdWyv, FlyWyv, BrtWyv, PscWyv, Levthn, FngWyv, FngBst, EldDrg, Lynian, Herbvr, Nptron, Fish -- and `species` is the same species written out by the game, off the Monster List volume item the row points at ("Flying Wyverns Vol 1" -> Flying Wyverns); volumes named after one monster (Deviljho, Plesioth) are dropped, and Fish, whose only volume carries its own monster's name, keeps the abbreviation. `speciesFrom` is "list" for a monster with its own row, or how the ROM ties it to one; `listSection` (0 small, 1 large, 2 elder, 3) and `listRank` (1-6) come from that row, and are null for a monster taking another's species.
